## GitHub Issues 

GitHub Issues are a way to track tasks, questions, problems, and ideas within a GitHub repository.

Think of them as a built-in task management and discussion system for a project.

## GitHub Issues{.smaller} 

| Use | Example |
|---|---|
| Report a problem (bug) | "The code in Exercise 3 produces an error." |
| Suggest an improvement | "Add another example of a `group_by()` operation." |
| Ask a question | "Why are we using `pivot_longer()` here?" |
| Track a task | "Complete the data visualization section." |
| Collaborate | "Review the analysis of missing data." |

Let's demonstrate!

Note: You will receive a GitHub notification if you are assigned an issue.

## Merge Conflicts 

A merge conflict occurs when a version control system, like Git, is unable to automatically combine changes from different branches during a merge operation because they have conflicting edits to the same part of a file..

.. in short: If you make changes to your document + pull changes from your repo that impact the changes you made… you will get a merge conflict

## Extension Questions{.smaller}

The Portland Trailblazers are a National Basketball Association (NBA)
sports team. These data reflect the points scored by 9 Portland
Trailblazers players across the first 10 games of the 2021-2022 NBA
season.

Download the `trailblazer.csv` roster. Add this to your data folder in
the data-viz project, and upload these data into R. Our goal is to
re-create the following image (see next slide)

## Question 

I want to explore these data, and make a data visualization that: 

-- Shows the points scored for each player

-- Shows if they did this on the road or at home 

-- I want to be able to also compare how they are doing over time

## 

```{r}
#| echo: false 
trailblazer <- read_csv("data/trailblazer21.csv")

new.blazer <- trailblazer |>  # save object as new.blazer
  pivot_longer( #make data longer
    cols = -Player, #bring all cols but Player down
    names_to = "Game", #name the col Game
    values_to = "Points", #name the values col Points
  ) |> 
  separate_wider_delim(Game , delim = "_", names = c("Game" , "Location"))

ggplot(
  new.blazer,
  aes(x = Game, y = Points, color = Location, group = 1)
) +
  geom_line(color = "gray70") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ Player) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Home" = "steelblue",
      "Away" = "darkorange"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trail Blazers Player Performance Across Games",
    x = "Game",
    y = "Points Scored",
    color = "Location"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```
